en: Bats are the only mammals capable of true, sustained flight.
Mango trees make their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide through photosynthesis, not from soil nutrients.
Taste buds for sweet, sour, salty, and bitter are distributed evenly across the entire human tongue.
Goldfish can actually remember things and learn tricks for up to five months, not just three seconds.
Brain scans show that humans use virtually all parts of their brain throughout the day, not just ten percent.
Philippine tarantulas have eight legs and two body segments, making them arachnids rather than six-legged insects.
Chameleons primarily change skin color to regulate body temperature and communicate emotions, rather than just to blend into their surroundings.
Human blood is always red, appearing blue in veins only because of how light penetrates and reflects off the skin.
Whale sharks breathe through gills and have skeletons made of cartilage, classifying them as fish rather than ocean-dwelling mammals.
Mature sunflowers permanently face east and stop tracking the sun, unlike young sunflower buds that do follow it.
Handling a Philippine wrinkled frog will not give you warts, which are actually caused by the human papillomavirus.
Butterflies actually taste their food using chemical sensors located on their feet, not on their mouthparts.
